title: Resilient call orchestration: SDK presets with opaque id rotation and tenant-aware backoff
creator: Asha Kumar
description: Goal: Define and implement a small set of cross-language SDK presets and helpers that make it easy to choose a safe, predictable retry/backoff profile and rotate opaque idempotency keys automatically for long-running streams or chunked requests. This ticket covers design decisions, per-language ergonomics (Python/TS/Go), and a short reference implementation for each SDK.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc with clear taxonomy mapping common transport and model errors to retryability categories (transient, throttling, permanent).
Three SDK presets implemented: failfast (low retries), balanced (default), throughput (aggressive batching, fewer short backoffs).
Opaque id rotation helper available in SDKs that can be opt-in for streaming/resumable uploads and documents explicit eviction window semantics.
Integration tests covering retry behavior for HTTP 5xx, gRPC UNAVAILABLE, rate-limit responses with Retry-After, and model-level non-deterministic errors.
Documentation and examples for migrating existing clients to presets and for choosing the right preset by latency/cost/SLO trade-offs.
implementation_notes: Key ideas: 1) Keep presets as small, well-documented structs (max_retries, base_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms, jitter_percent, retryable_error_codes, id_rotation_policy) so language bindings can map them to idiomatic constructs. 2) Id rotation: provide an OpaqueIdProvider that rotates after N seconds or after X bytes/tokens; default N=300s for streaming to limit duplicate work window. 3) Streaming semantics: support a resume token + idempotency header pair; when resume token lost, SDK falls back to start-with-rotation. 4) Telemetry: emit events on each retry including reason, backoff chosen, and id rotation occurrences for downstream billing/cost analysis.
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Drafted taxonomy for retryable vs non-retryable errors; initial mapping includes HTTP 408/429/5xx as retryable-with-jitter, gRPC UNAVAILABLE/RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED as retryable; model-internal errors flagged as 'investigate' and default to conservative retry. (Asha)
2026-02-18: Spike implemented in python-sdk repo: OpaqueIdProvider and a Preset enum. Basic tests for HTTP 500 + Retry-After pass locally. (Benji)

2026-02-25: Design review with PM and DX. Feedback: make defaults tenant-aware (enterprise customers prefer smaller retry windows to avoid duplicate processing) and expose a simple opt-out. Action: add tenant_hint to client constructor. (Claire)
2026-03-03: TypeScript SDK ergonomic notes added; recommend Promise-based retry wrapper with cancellation tokens for failfast preset. (Emily)
2026-03-08: Cross-language sync: aligned on naming for presets and id rotation constants. Preparing PRs for python/ts/go. (Benji)
testing_plan: Unit tests per SDK that stub transport layers to simulate HTTP 429 with Retry-After, intermittent 503 spikes, and gRPC UNAVAILABLE. Integration tests in staging that validate: (1) presets produce expected retry counts under controlled failure injection, (2) id rotation helper reduces duplicate processing for resumed streams, (3) telemetry events emitted with correct tags. Load test for throughput preset to ensure it doesn't overwhelm serving pool under backpressure.
rollout_plan: Feature gated via a client-side flag disabled by default for existing apps. Step 1: release SDKs with presets behind 'new_retry_presets' feature flag. Step 2: opt-in beta customers (2 enterprise, 10 projects) and monitor retry telemetry and error regressions for 2 weeks. Step 3: enable as default for new SDK versions if no regressions. Rollback: client can opt-out by setting preset to 'legacy' which maps to existing behavior.
open_questions: What should be the default opaque id rotation window for on-prem/private deployments where clocks may drift?
Should we include a token-budget-aware guard that reduces retries when remaining token quota is low?
How to represent model-internal transient errors in a stable cross-sdk contract (model error codes are noisy)?
notes_from_review: PM Claire asked to explicitly call out customer migration path and create a short FAQ explaining duplicate-response implications when enabling more aggressive retries. Security raised a minor concern about id rotation entropy for multi-tenant keys; follow-up with Security team scheduled. (Benji)
migration_guidance: For existing clients: 1) Try 'balanced' preset in staging and validate idempotent operations. 2) For streaming uploads, enable OpaqueIdProvider with small rotation window (60s) in dev to validate resume behavior. 3) If downstream systems cannot tolerate duplicates, use 'failfast' or instrument server-side dedup using the id header. Provide sample snippets in each SDK repo.
